what_it_is: Ouroboros (MIT) is a spec-first 'Agent OS'. It has about 358K lines of Python in src/, about 497K lines of tests, and a small Rust TUI. An MCP server, a set of skills, and an orchestrator wrap 14 host coding CLIs, including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and Antigravity/agy, and spawn them as worker subprocesses with permissions forcibly bypassed. The loop runs as follows: a Socratic interview gated by an LLM-scored ambiguity number; a Seed that is immutable in memory, whose acceptance criteria can carry hidden verify_command/output_assertion graders; parallel AC execution with evidence checks (typed claims against the transcript, sandboxed replay, workspace digests) and a frozen pre-dispatch check package with held-out oracle cases admitted red-before-green on the base checkout (on by default, but only constructible on codex/claude runtimes); and a 3-stage evaluation in which only executed Stage-1 checks can grant approval while model stages can only withhold. 'Gets smarter on its own' concretely means that Wonder/Reflect LLMs rewrite a lineage's Seed (goal, constraints, AC wording, ontology) over up to 30 generations, with Ralph chains of 1-10. It does not mean the system modifies its own prompts, skills or code, and there is no cross-run memory. The project does hold the line in places, but several paths still let a model certify completion (Ralph's QA pass, auto Seed-QA 'complete_verified', LLM-written regex verifiers, plugin-mode evaluation), and several 'no evidence' paths keep work as unverified success. State lives in an event-sourced SQLite store with guard tables and leases but no hash chain. The host hooks are thin, fail-open and advisory, so enforcement lives in the orchestrator, not in hooks.

atoms.name: Executed evidence grants; model review only withholds
atoms.statement: Final approval is computed in exactly one function, which returns false unless Stage-1 executed checks ran and all passed; every model stage (semantic, consensus, reward-hacking) can only withhold approval.
atoms.mechanism: decide_final_approval requires stage1_result.has_executed_evidence (models.py:578) and then asks model_review_withhold_reason whether any model stage withheld (models.py:526-563). The pipeline's only approval call is _build_result (pipeline.py:275), and no caller can pass an approval in. Injected text in a judge prompt can therefore at most suppress a veto; it can never mint an approval.
atoms.proof_purpose: Completion cannot result from any model output: a task is complete only if every check G1 executed passed and no veto fired.
atoms.g1_design: The Stop gate computes complete = (all contract checks executed by G1 passed and bound to a receipt) AND (veto set empty). Judge outputs are typed as veto-only inputs, and no schema field or code path lets them contribute an approval. Port the exhaustive 'no combination of model verdicts approves without executed evidence' test as a G1 conformance test.

atoms.name: Tri-state acceptance; skipped check is not evidence
atoms.statement: Each Stage-1 result is classified once as EXECUTED_PASS, EXECUTED_FAIL or NO_EVIDENCE. A skipped or never-run check is never evidence, so outcomes are APPROVED, REJECTED or UNVERIFIED.
atoms.mechanism: MechanicalResult.disposition returns EXECUTED_FAIL if any executed check failed, and EXECUTED_PASS only if every check passed and at least one ran; otherwise it returns NO_EVIDENCE (models.py:176-188). derive_acceptance_state maps NO_EVIDENCE to UNVERIFIED (models.py:589-603; core/acceptance.py:13-28). The run-level aggregate is APPROVED only if every criterion is APPROVED (models.py:606).
atoms.proof_purpose: In every receipt, absence of executed verification is distinguishable from a pass.
atoms.g1_design: Receipts carry an executed flag per check. Any check that has executed=false or is missing output leaves the task UNVERIFIED (still open), never complete. 'Skipped' must never render as pass in projections either.

atoms.name: Aggregate verdict recomputed from literal per-check results
atoms.statement: A stored aggregate 'passed' flag is never trusted: it is reconciled, failing closed, to the conjunction of every check's literal True, and an empty checklist never counts as all-passed.
atoms.mechanism: MechanicalResult.__post_init__ recomputes passed as (self.passed is True and every c.passed is True) and overwrites an aggregate that disagrees (models.py:146-158). checklist.all_passed returns False when the checklist is empty (checklist.py:76-82).
atoms.proof_purpose: A receipt's summary verdict can be derived from its per-check results and cannot contradict them.
atoms.g1_design: When G1 reads or replays a receipt, it recomputes the summary from the per-check tuples (exit code, expected output digest). A receipt whose stored summary differs is rejected, and an empty check vector is never 'all pass'.

atoms.name: Judge-reported reward-hacking risk as veto
atoms.statement: The Stage-2 semantic LLM is told to look for hardcoded outputs, test-only branches and placeholder logic and to report a reward_hacking_risk; a value of 0.7 or more withholds approval, but an omitted field defaults to 0.0.
atoms.mechanism: The 'Anti-Gaming Verification' prompt section is at semantic.py:192-199. The parser defaults a missing risk to 0.0 and clamps the value (semantic.py:269-278), and the veto fires at REWARD_HACKING_VETO_THRESHOLD = 0.7 (models.py:34, 553-563). The semantic-evaluator system prompt's 'exact format' omits the risk field entirely (semantic-evaluator.md:3).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 3-tier hooks Stop audit with a fast judge model
principle_conflict: Z3: it relies on model reasoning, which is acceptable only as an extra veto
P8: a judge proves no fact; it only adds suspicion, so it needs a named purpose to exist
atoms.proof_purpose: none (it can only add a veto; it proves no fact)
atoms.g1_design: If G1 keeps a judge, it should be veto-only and fail closed: a missing or unparseable verdict counts as a veto, bounded by the Stop continuation budget. Worker artifacts go to the judge as nonce-delimited quoted data, and a judge pass never counts toward completion.

atoms.name: Advisory multi-model consensus and deliberative jury
atoms.statement: Stage 3 runs a 2/3 vote across models, or one model with three role prompts when no OpenRouter key is set, plus a deliberative advocate/devil/judge mode that nothing in production calls; the vote can only withhold, and reviewer independence is a vendor label that gates nothing.
atoms.mechanism: The majority threshold is 0.66 with at least 2 votes (consensus.py:139, 395), with a single-model fallback (consensus.py:310). Triggers are evaluated in trigger.py:133. Vendor filtering never drops below 2 voters and only produces a label (reviewer_independence.py:170). A consensus rejection is the first withholding reason checked (models.py:539).
principle_conflict: P7: puts multiple vendors/providers next to the authority path
P8: no unique proof purpose; G1 runs a single host model (Gemini Flash), so a jury would be mostly self-review
Mathematics placement: ensembles belong to measurement, not to the authority path
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Not in the authority path. Ensembles may appear only in G1's measurement harness.

atoms.name: Agent-writable check config, interpreter and PATH
atoms.statement: Stage-1 commands come from .ouroboros/mechanical.toml inside the evaluated tree; if the file is absent an LLM writes it, and it is never re-detected. The commands run with the checkout's .venv/bin first on PATH, so the agent under evaluation can redefine or shim its own grader, and any executed 'python -c pass' counts as evidence.
atoms.mechanism: The config path is working_dir/.ouroboros/mechanical.toml (languages.py:138), and an existing file is reused as-is (detector.py:164). with_project_venv prepends the checkout venv (core/project_env.py:90; mechanical.py:120). The coverage threshold applies only when output parses (mechanical.py:261), and a trivial command still yields final_approved (test_pipeline_acceptance_authority.py:196).
principle_conflict: Z2/Z5: the agent shapes the evidence that grants approval
P4: the verification definition is not owned by the harness
P4: Stage-1 checks are project-wide and not tied to a criterion, so approval can be vacuous for a given AC
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: check definitions, interpreters and runner config live in G1's root-of-trust store outside workspacePaths and are pinned by hash. PreToolUse denies writes to the contract's protected paths, and G1 never resolves executables through the workspace PATH or venv.

atoms.name: Allowlist and operator filter for check commands
atoms.statement: Commands loaded from config must use an allowlisted executable and contain no shell operators or absolute/home paths, and python may run only as -m on stdlib or declared modules.
atoms.mechanism: _ALLOWED_EXECUTABLES is at languages.py:37. Shell operators are rejected at languages.py:189 and executable names checked at languages.py:206. The stdlib-runnable module list for python -m is at detector.py:1859.
principle_conflict: P8: an allowlist is weaker than pinning the exact argv and binary hash; keep it only if contracts accept model-proposed commands
atoms.proof_purpose: A contract check command is a single argv with no shell composition.
atoms.g1_design: At contract admission, reject any check command that is not a plain argv (no shell operators, no workspace-relative interpreter) and record the resolved binary hash (see OUR-22).

atoms.name: Grader command never reaches the worker
atoms.statement: Each AC's verify_command and output_assertion are withheld from every worker prompt, retry and host-dispatch payload; the worker sees only its expected_artifacts and a note that the harness verifies independently.
atoms.mechanism: The success-contract block surfaces only the part of the contract the worker owns (atomic_prompt_builder.py:34-55, 125-129), and host dispatch sends the same prompt without assertions (host_dispatch.py:36-38). The boundary covers transport only, not the filesystem (implementation.md:97-103), and verify_command is persisted in event payloads that the worker's user can read (parallel_executor.py:9980).
atoms.proof_purpose: The agent could not tailor its output to the check text, because that text never entered its context or any file it can read.
atoms.g1_design: Check definitions live only in G1's root-of-trust directory outside workspacePaths and are never sent through injectSteps. PreToolUse denies any tool call whose arguments reference that directory or the G1 ledger. Injected context names only AC ids and required artifacts.

atoms.name: Sanitized retry hints instead of raw grader output
atoms.statement: Retry guidance is built from missing artifacts, sanitized verifier output and trace facts, with every encoding variant of hidden values removed longest-first; output tails and the names of failing claims still reach the worker.
atoms.mechanism: hidden_contract_variants and transformed-value detection (contract_redaction.py:13, 265) feed build_assertion_safe_retry_hint (retry_hints.py:88), which still includes verifier output tails (retry_hints.py:120).
principle_conflict: P8: redaction deny-lists grow with every new encoding; not forwarding the output at all is simpler and complete
atoms.proof_purpose: Stop-continuation reasons cannot leak the hidden check.
atoms.g1_design: Build Stop 'continue' reasons only from structured fields G1 owns: failing AC ids, the pass/fail vector, Hamming distance and artifact names. Never echo raw check stdout/stderr, so no redaction list is needed.

atoms.name: Process-local opaque Seed handle vault
atoms.statement: For plugin dispatch, the raw Seed stays in an in-memory vault keyed by an opaque handle that is bound to one session and consumed once; a server restart invalidates the handle and evaluation then fails closed.
atoms.mechanism: project_worker_safe_seed drops verifier keys and redacts their values (seed_handoff.py:83). The vault is a bounded LRU of opaque handles (seed_handoff.py:167), and handles do not survive a restart (architecture.md:43).
principle_conflict: P1/P3: state that dies with a process cannot support a fresh agent continuing the work
agy hooks are short-lived processes that share no memory
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Use a root-of-trust file store outside the workspace instead (OUR-08).

atoms.name: Held-out oracle cases frozen before work
atoms.statement: Before the worker starts, a read-only constructor model writes per-criterion oracles with visible and held-out cases. Held-out values are never written to disk or shown to the worker, the per-attempt gate uses visible cases only, and held-out cases run once at terminal verification. A package PASS from these model-authored oracles accepts a criterion even over a legacy rejection.
atoms.mechanism: Held-out status is the constructor's own per-case declaration (oracle.py:52-55), at least one is required (oracle.py:322), and oracle files are never materialized (admission.py:318). The gate runs visible cases only (authority.py:555), an interrupted terminal run never re-runs held-out cases (authority.py:940), and a reference implementation from the same model filters out inconsistent cases (reference_check.py:253). A PASS is accepted at acceptance.py:466 and 796, including over a legacy rejection (test_acceptance.py:205).
principle_conflict: Z1/Z4: expected values and held-out labels are model output, and their pass certifies acceptance
doc-vs-code: the constructor prompt demands two held-out cases (check-constructor.md:41) but the code requires one (oracle.py:322)
atoms.proof_purpose: The work satisfies inputs the agent never saw.
atoms.g1_design: G1 may keep user- or G1-authored hidden cases in the root-of-trust store and run them at Stop. Model-generated hidden cases may only veto; they are never the sole passing evidence for an AC row.

atoms.name: Checks must fail on base, pass after
atoms.statement: A reproduction check is admitted only if it fails, with its own structured failure signature, on a fresh copy of the base checkout. A check that already passes on base, or whose held-out cases all pass on base, is excluded as non-discriminating, and a preservation check must pass on base.
atoms.mechanism: _classify handles this (admission.py:353-403): preservation checks must pass on base (393), a reproduction that passes on base is VIOLATED (397-398), and a seen signature with every held-out case passing on base is held_out_not_discriminating (399-400). A terminal PASS additionally requires that a held-out case which failed on base now passes (acceptance.py:439).
atoms.proof_purpose: The check discriminates: it fails on the pre-task tree and passes on the delivered tree, so the work caused the pass.
atoms.g1_design: When a task contract is registered, G1 snapshots the base tree and runs each AC check on a copy. A check is admitted only if it fails with its declared signature (reproduction) or passes (preservation). An AC row with no admitted discriminating check is a zero row, and the contract is rejected.

atoms.name: Canary proves the check exercises its target
atoms.statement: A test command is trusted only if it exits 0 on two base copies and fails after its target file is replaced with bytes that no language parses.
atoms.mechanism: The admission design is described at target_commands.py:37-45 and implemented by judge_admission (target_commands.py:424-450), which _admit applies during base regression (base_regression.py:1133-1153).
atoms.proof_purpose: The check is not vacuous: its result depends on the file it claims to test.
atoms.g1_design: For each AC check that names target files, G1 runs a one-time canary at admission: it corrupts the target in a scratch copy and requires the check to fail. The canary result is recorded in the admission receipt.

atoms.name: Pre-existing tests rerun from base bytes
atoms.statement: Base tests that pair with or import changed modules run twice on the base and once on a copy of the candidate, in which those tests and their conftests are restored to base bytes and the worker's pytest config is neutralized. A test that passes stably on base but fails twice on the candidate is a veto.
atoms.mechanism: Selection is at base_regression.py:322-437, config neutralization at 654-679, the candidate run with restored tests at 1047-1131, and the stability rule at 706-724. The check is veto-only, decides only when a package was admitted (239-250), and defaults to 'decide' (169), but any error becomes 'no observation' (897-898). Footprint exemptions come from records the candidate's own processes write (footprint.py:33).
principle_conflict: P4: errors in this check become no observation and do not block (base_regression.py:897)
Z5: footprint exemptions are written by processes the candidate controls
atoms.proof_purpose: Pre-existing tests, in their original bytes, still pass against the new code, so deleting or editing tests cannot hide a regression.
atoms.g1_design: At Stop, G1 verification also runs the pre-task test files, restored from the base snapshot, against a copy of the candidate tree. A test that passed stably on base and now fails is a veto. Errors in this check block completion, and no candidate-written exemptions are accepted.

atoms.name: Per-check exclusion with coverage recomputation
atoms.statement: A role violation or indeterminate result excludes only that check. Coverage is then recomputed, so a criterion keeps authority only while some admitted check still covers it, and one replacement model call targets the uncovered criteria.
atoms.mechanism: Exclusion reasons are listed at per_check.py:68 and criteria_without_admitted_check is at per_check.py:241-272. Replacement targets come from coverage.py:114-190, and the journal reducer re-derives the coverage rule from the frozen manifest (ledger.py:283).
principle_conflict: P4: there is no zero-row rejection; uncovered criteria fall back to the legacy verifier and can be accepted without evidence (OUR-16)
atoms.proof_purpose: After exclusions, every acceptance-criterion row of the coverage matrix still has at least one admitted deterministic check.
atoms.g1_design: Build G1's coverage matrix exactly this way (AC x admitted checks, recomputed after exclusions), but reject the contract on any zero row instead of falling back. A replacement check is a new contract version, not a silent patch.

atoms.name: No evidence becomes unverified success
atoms.statement: When transcript verification is unavailable, when the verify gate times out or cannot start, or when neither the check package nor the legacy verifier has evidence, the AC or criterion is kept successful and labelled unverified, and a worker can trigger the timeout path.
atoms.mechanism: UNAVAILABLE failure classes map to ACCEPT (verifier.py:108), and the executor clears the rejection when the verifier is unavailable (parallel_executor.py:9195-9208; test at test_parallel_executor.py:9364). A verify-gate timeout is quarantined: success is kept and transcript checks are skipped (parallel_executor.py:9830, 12749-12750; test at verify_by_default.py:3192). The boundary accepts unverified criteria when the legacy verifier has no evidence (acceptance.py:62-66, 796; test_authority_oracle.py:448), and seed_verify_gate.py:5-7 states this as the design.
principle_conflict: P4: work is completed without deterministic verification
Z7: absence of proof is treated as acceptable
exploitable: making the code under test hang past verify_command_timeout_seconds earns quarantine instead of failure
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Keep the 'preserve work' intent by recording the work in the ledger as UNVERIFIED and leaving the task open. For completion, timeouts, missing transcripts and unavailable verifiers count as FAIL, and they consume Stop budget.

atoms.name: Typed claims checked against tool-call transcript
atoms.statement: The worker must emit a fenced JSON evidence record (files_touched, commands_run, tests_passed). The terminal self-report is excluded by identity, and each claim must be backed by structured tool calls; otherwise the verdict is FABRICATION_SUSPECTED, unless every gap is a recognized EVIDENCE_FORM_MISMATCH.
atoms.mechanism: extract_evidence parses one fenced JSON object (evidence_schema.py:191-221), and the terminal self-report is excluded by identity (evidence/verification.py:84-90). commands_run is matched only against structured Bash tool_input (claims.py:200-253). The FABRICATION vs FORM_MISMATCH decision is at verification.py:277-307, with its semantics documented at verifier-evidence-policy.md:366-380.
principle_conflict: P2: it forces the agent to emit a custom evidence format, changing native behavior
Z5: several support tiers still read text the model wrote (OUR-18)
atoms.proof_purpose: Every claimed command corresponds to a host-recorded tool call that succeeded.
atoms.g1_design: G1 does not ask the agent for claims. It records its own PostToolUse facts (tool, args digest, exit status, call id). If the agent's final message claims tests or commands, G1 cross-checks the claim against those facts only to label FABRICATION vs FORM_MISMATCH in the continuation reason.

atoms.name: Narration and stdout accepted as evidence
atoms.statement: Several support tiers accept text the model controls: assistant narration or echoed stdout can back files_touched, regexes over worker-produced output can back tests_passed, and a 'functional tier' accepts any workspace script that exits 0, even on prose ACs.
atoms.mechanism: File proof is read from the full text of any message (claims.py:424, 1670), and test success is detected by regexes over output (test_detection.py:198). The functional tier is at test_detection.py:705 and verification.py:225, and regex-based AC classification can drop required fields (ac_classification.py:175). A print('ok') script backs tests_passed in tests (test_observed_runs.py:320; test_functional_command_tier.py:421).
principle_conflict: Z4/Z5: model output and evidence the model presented are treated as proof
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: G1 evidence is limited to host-recorded tool events and checks G1 ran itself. Assistant prose and the content of tool stdout are never evidence of completion.

atoms.name: Harness replays commands in isolated copies
atoms.statement: The harness re-runs up to three allowlisted transcript commands in a fresh copy of the workspace, with an environment built from scratch and under the sandbox. A replay counts only if it exits 0 without timing out, its exit matches the transcript's, and no pre-existing file's SHA-256 changed.
atoms.mechanism: Candidates are selected at command_replay.py:459-543, capped at 3 (test_reexecution.py:22). A protected SHA-256 digest is taken before and after (command_replay.py:651, 738), and success is judged by the predicate at harness_observation.py:122-128. Observations must be in-memory harness objects (harness_observation.py:276), and the denylist covers the whole launcher chain (replay_policy.py:1085).
principle_conflict: P4: replaying the agent's own commands verifies only what the agent chose to run; G1 should run its own contract checks
atoms.proof_purpose: The check G1 ran passed on an isolated copy of the exact tree without changing any pre-existing file.
atoms.g1_design: Reuse this runner shape for G1's own contract checks at Stop: copy the tree, use a scratch environment and the sandbox where available, take SHA-256 of pre-existing files before and after, and judge by exit code only. Record the tree digest, argv, binary hash, exit code and output digests in the receipt.

atoms.name: Narrowing options and environment disqualify evidence
atoms.statement: Any option or environment assignment that selects, excludes or reconfigures tests disables claim linkage, for example pytest -k/--deselect/-p/-c, PYTHONPATH, JEST_* or go test -run. Configuration carried inside the workspace, such as pytest.ini addopts or conftest.py, is explicitly not detected.
atoms.mechanism: Option tables are at replay_policy.py:382 and NARROWING_ENVIRONMENT at replay_policy.py:639, and exports made in earlier Bash calls also count (test_detection.py:884). The policy and its stated scope gap are at verifier-evidence-policy.md:235 and 320.
principle_conflict: P8: an ever-growing deny-list; G1 avoids it by owning the exact argv and pinning runner config
atoms.proof_purpose: The check ran the full declared test set, not a narrowed subset.
atoms.g1_design: G1 runs contract checks with a fixed argv and isolated runner configuration, using an explicit config file from the root of trust. Runner-config files in the workspace (pytest.ini, conftest.py, jest.config.*) are either part of the protected contract scope or restored from base when pre-existing tests run.

atoms.name: Probed write and network sandbox, fail-closed
atoms.statement: Commands the controller runs on its own authority are confined: Landlock ABI 3 or later plus seccomp and a network namespace on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS, AppContainer on Windows. A per-process mutation-matrix probe runs first, and nothing runs if confinement or network isolation is unavailable; however, the sandbox can be switched off and that state is not recorded in receipts.
atoms.mechanism: confine (exec_sandbox.py:960-1052) returns SandboxUnavailable when no backend exists (1012-1021), after the probe at exec_sandbox.py:676 and _sandbox_probe.py:31. The Linux helper requires MIN_LANDLOCK_ABI = 3 (_confine_exec.py:131), filters metadata syscalls with seccomp (492) and checks for loopback-only networking just before exec (686). The off switch is at config/exec_sandbox.py:35 and check_env.py:21, while the run display still claims confinement (run_wiring.py:914).
principle_conflict: P7: platform-specific; under PRoot-style hosts Landlock/seccomp/netns are likely unavailable, so this would fail closed and block all verification
P5: confinement state must be bound into the receipt, which Ouroboros does not do
atoms.proof_purpose: A verification run could not write outside its copy or reach the network.
atoms.g1_design: Probe once per host. If confinement is available, confine G1's check runs. Either way, record the sandbox backend and state in the receipt so a receipt from an unconfined run can be told apart, and never display confinement that was not applied.

atoms.name: Hash-pinned check executables, allowlisted environment
atoms.statement: Check interpreters are pinned by realpath plus SHA-256 and re-hashed from an O_NOFOLLOW descriptor right before exec (fexecve on Linux). The verify shell is sealed by realpath, SHA-256 and a capability probe, and replay and check environments are built from an allowlist rather than copied.
atoms.mechanism: pin_interpreter is at check_env.py:201-217, the check_command launch at 251-308 and re-verification at _pinned_exec.py:38-76. The bash seal is at verify_shell.py:213-280, and the environment allowlists at exec_sandbox.py:271 and command_replay.py:171. Gaps: the pin covers the binary only (check_env.py:58), and the hidden verify gate and vendor CLIs inherit the controller environment (verify_shell.py:441; child_env.py:67).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 verification that the harness runs itself in a scrubbed environment (adds binary-hash pinning at exec time)
atoms.proof_purpose: The check ran with exactly the executable bytes recorded at admission, in an environment G1 constructed.
atoms.g1_design: Contract admission records the SHA-256 of each check executable. At Stop, G1 re-hashes before exec (fexecve or O_NOFOLLOW where possible), builds the environment from an allowlist, and writes the binary hash and environment digest into the receipt. It never prepends a workspace venv or bin directory to PATH.

atoms.name: Tree digest brackets every write-capable step
atoms.statement: The workspace content digest is taken before and after any model step with write authority, such as the level coordinator. The model's own 'fixed it' summary is explicitly not proof, any change forces re-verification of work already accepted, and an unreadable digest fails closed.
atoms.mechanism: Digests are taken around the coordinator (parallel_executor.py:4692-4740), with a fallback that treats any Write/Edit/Bash message as possible mutation (5030-5044), and revalidation runs at 4850-4870. _workspace_content_digest returns None on read failure so callers fail closed (5047), the coordinator's self-reported conflicts_resolved only labels (coordinator.py:1219), and settlement replays when the digest moved (5387). Gap: the digest skips git-ignored paths and .venv, and .gitignore is agent-writable (5087; 1784).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding the current source and tree (adds before/after bracketing of each actor)
atoms.proof_purpose: The tree that was verified is the tree delivered; nothing changed between verification and completion.
atoms.g1_design: Each verification receipt records a tree digest, and G1 recomputes it at completion; any PostToolUse write after the receipt invalidates it. The digest scope comes from the contract in the root of trust, never from an agent-editable .gitignore.

atoms.name: One-to-one call-id correlation, fail-closed
atoms.statement: A tool event counts only when its start is correlated by call id with its own successful completion: duplicate starts cannot share one completion, a malformed error bit cannot be laundered by a 'completed' status, and correlation conflicts fail closed. The IOJournal that records these pairs swallows append failures.
atoms.mechanism: Success evidence with call-id correlation is checked at claims.py:1576-1667. Paired started/returned I/O events are created at events/io.py:270. IOJournal append failures are swallowed (io_recorder.py:393-409).
principle_conflict: P4: an evidence journal that swallows append failures is fail-open
atoms.proof_purpose: Each recorded tool result belongs to exactly one tool call that G1 saw being requested.
atoms.g1_design: PreToolUse logs (conversationId, stepIdx, tool, args digest), and PostToolUse must match exactly one open entry; unmatched or duplicated results are not evidence. An append failure makes that step non-evidence for completion while staying fail-open for the agent.

atoms.name: Content-addressed evidence handles and set membership
atoms.statement: Evidence journal entries get content-addressed handles: a SHA-256 over kind, payload and source event ids. The deliver gate accepts a claim only if every cited (fact, chunk) pair belongs to the harness's set and the claim's terms appear in the cited text, but in production it only observes.
atoms.mechanism: The stable handle is computed at journal.py:176-211 and set-membership validation is at traceguard_validator.py:101-203. The claim-term guard is at claim_term_guard.py:63-164 and evaluate_deliver_claim at deliver_gate.py:1316-1464. Production enforces a HARD RULE that it is observe-only (parallel_executor.py:9584).
principle_conflict: P8: the claim-matching half exists to check agent claims, which G1 does not accept
atoms.proof_purpose: A receipt cites its evidence by hash, so any edited evidence no longer matches its handle.
atoms.g1_design: Keep only the handle scheme: every observation G1 stores in the ledger gets sha256(kind, payload, source ids), and completion receipts list the handles they rely on.

atoms.name: Every criterion needs a deterministic check
atoms.statement: Before a run, every acceptance criterion must declare either a verify_command or an explicit per-AC verify_exemption_reason, but the default mode only warns, and an unreadable config also falls back to warn.
atoms.mechanism: unverifiable_criteria is at seed_verify_gate.py:37-48, and mode resolution falls back to 'warn' (seed_verify_gate.py:73-84). The gate is applied at session preparation (runner.py:8571-8612), the default is 'warn' (config/models.py:822), and the exemption field is defined at seed.py:554. Auto preflight reports the same finding as advisory only (seed_preflight.py:1761).
principle_conflict: P4: warns by default and resolves its mode fail-open
Z1: the verify_command itself is usually written by the seed-architect model
atoms.proof_purpose: Every acceptance-criterion row of the contract has at least one deterministic check.
atoms.g1_design: G1's contract check only blocks and fails closed: a zero row (no admitted check) rejects the contract. An exemption removes that AC from what completion may claim, and the receipt lists it.

atoms.name: Content-derived per-AC keys, random seed id
atoms.statement: Each AC gets a semantic key: SHA-256 of its description, verify_command, artifacts and assertion, truncated to 16 hex characters. The Seed id, however, is a random uuid, and Seed YAML on disk is trusted on load and on resume.
atoms.mechanism: derive_semantic_ac_key is at seed.py:730-753, the uuid seed_id at seed.py:421 and the frozen model at seed.py:768. On REVIEW resume the on-disk Seed replaces the Seed held in state (auto/pipeline.py:1020), and revising an AC keeps the parent's contract (acceptance_contracts.py:51). Only the boundary package hashes the full Seed (package.py:627).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 immutable task contracts with a contract hash
principle_conflict: P3: a random id plus trusted on-disk YAML lets the content change under the same identity
atoms.proof_purpose: An AC and its check are the same ones that were admitted; any edit produces a new AC identity.
atoms.g1_design: Keep T1's contract hash and add per-AC keys = sha256(AC text, check argv, expected artifacts) so receipts bind each row's identity. Never accept an identity from a mutable file without re-hashing.

atoms.name: Recorded decision valid only for exact Seed
atoms.statement: Formal evaluation reuses a recorded check-package decision only if its package was frozen for the exact Seed digest and the decision names the Seed's criteria in Seed order; anything else is no evidence, never a pass.
atoms.mechanism: recorded_criterion_decisions checks the projection's seed_digest (decision.py:40) and the order of criterion keys (decision.py:48). evidence_for_criteria maps decisions into evaluation only on an exact match (evaluation_package_evidence.py:54).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding the receipt sequence and hash
atoms.proof_purpose: A verification result is applied only to the exact contract it was produced for.
atoms.g1_design: T1 already does this. Keep the rule 'a mismatch is no evidence, never a pass' explicit in G1's receipt check.

atoms.name: Spec-controlled and fail-off verification switches
atoms.statement: A Seed can opt out of verify-by-default with execution_mode: legacy, which accepts every root AC on self-report. Plugin dispatch silently downgrades verify-by-default, and the check-package switch treats unparsable environment values and unreadable config as 'off'.
atoms.mechanism: The legacy branch is in _resolve_fat_harness_mode (cli/commands/run.py:485-503), and the plugin downgrade is in execution_handlers.py:423-443. The legacy path accepts all root ACs (runner.py:9898). Switch precedence and the fail-off cases are at switch.py:59-76.
principle_conflict: P4: the task contract, often written by a model, can disable verification
Z6: an ambiguous operator setting resolves to the weaker mode
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: verification policy comes only from G1's root of trust and is immutable per task. No contract field can weaken it, and unparsable or unreadable safety settings resolve to the strict mode.

atoms.name: Workspace-sourced config cannot change execution
atoms.statement: A project-local .env, which travels with a cloned repo, may not set executable paths, runtime selectors, permission modes, preload hooks, package-manager or module-resolution variables, git process controls, the sandbox switch or the verify shell; only home and global sources are trusted.
atoms.mechanism: The rationale and seven classes of sinks are documented at untrusted_env.py:14-53. UNTRUSTED_ENV_DENYLIST (untrusted_env.py:54) includes OUROBOROS_VERIFY_BASH (103) and OUROBOROS_EXEC_SANDBOX (256).
atoms.proof_purpose: Every policy value in force came from the global root-of-trust file, not from files the agent can write in the workspace.
atoms.g1_design: Treat .agents/hooks.json and any G1 config in the workspace as untrusted. The global ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json is the root of trust, and workspace hooks may only add denies. At SessionStart, G1 verifies its policy digest against the global anchor.

atoms.name: LLM-scored ambiguity gate with bypasses
atoms.statement: Interview completion and Seed generation are gated on ambiguity = 1 - sum(weight x LLM clarity) <= 0.2. Deterministic code only clamps and applies floors, and several paths skip the gate: a force flag, a plugin path that accepts a caller-supplied score, a magic answer prefix that closes the interview unscored, and a typed-evidence alternative that is never wired in.
atoms.mechanism: Constants and weights are at ambiguity.py:37-59 and the formula at ambiguity.py:836-852. The scorer's transcript is built from raw rounds with no untrusted-data framing (ambiguity.py:603). The force bypass is at seed_generator.py:1675, the plugin path's caller-supplied score at authoring_handlers.py:1296-1309, the safe-default synthesis prefix at authoring_handlers.py:273 and 2881-2905, and the unwired evidence ledger at ambiguity_evidence.py:1.
principle_conflict: Z1/Z3/Z4: a model's number certifies readiness
PH: improving input clarity is not G1's job
P2: an interview replaces the native agent flow
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Not adopted. At most it is a measurement signal in G1's A/B harness.

atoms.name: Answer provenance from forgeable text prefixes
atoms.statement: Answer provenance is decided by bracketed prefixes in the answer text: [from-code], [from-repo], [from-research] and [from-data] count as observations, and everything else, including [from-auto] machine answers, carries user-confirmed authority.
atoms.mechanism: OBSERVATION_PREFIXES is at answer_provenance.py:43-82. Answers that are not observations become USER_STATEMENT candidates (requirement_distillation.py:197-212). The ledger's source-to-provenance map labels canned defaults as user-confirmed or maintainer policy (auto/ledger.py:142-158), and these are exempt from the provenance gate (auto/grading.py:664).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct trusted channel versus data channel
principle_conflict: Z4/Z6: authority is read from in-band text the model writes
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: G1 derives provenance only from the hook channel (event type, conversationId, stepIdx), never from tags inside model or tool text.

atoms.name: LLM answers its own interview questions
atoms.statement: In ooo auto, an answer-refiner LLM ('You answer Socratic interview questions on the user's behalf') replaces canned answers. It runs on the same backend that scores ambiguity, and lateral 'stagnation concretization' text is pushed into the transcript to lower the score.
atoms.mechanism: The refiner system prompt is at auto/adapters.py:1236-1259. Refined values keep their original source tags (interview_driver.py:1711), and stagnation text is injected at interview_driver.py:1828. The refiner is wired in production at auto_handler.py:563.
principle_conflict: Z1: a model asks, a model answers and a model scores, forming a closed self-approval loop
Z6: the user's intent is simulated
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Not adopted.

atoms.name: Regex A-grade rubric with self-laundering repair
atoms.statement: The deterministic A-grade gate treats an AC as observable if it has a verify_command or its prose matches keyword/regex hints, and the bounded repairer rewrites failing ACs into a boilerplate sentence that the same regex accepts.
atoms.mechanism: The grade-A thresholds are at grading.py:470-488, and _OBSERVABLE_HINTS and _is_observable at grading.py:46 and 550-573. The replacement text is generated at seed_repairer.py:161 and 361-373, and the code itself calls it a placeholder proof phrase (execution_acceptance.py:750). In a test, a vague AC becomes grade A and the run starts (test_interview_pipeline.py:1222).
principle_conflict: P4: deterministic-looking checks over prose prove nothing about executable behavior
Z2: the system rewrites failing inputs until they pass its own gate
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: G1's contract check counts only admitted executable checks per AC (OUR-12, OUR-26), never text patterns.

atoms.name: Auto marks COMPLETE at dispatch
atoms.statement: ooo auto reaches COMPLETE as soon as the run starter returns a handle, and a passing static LLM Seed-QA verdict alone sets complete_verified.
atoms.mechanism: COMPLETE is set after the handoff (auto/pipeline.py:1440-1459). _has_verified_product_completion reads last_qa_passed (pipeline.py:2716-2731), which yields complete_verified (artifact_state.py:41-42). Seed QA is otherwise advisory (seed_qa_advisory.py:1), and Ralph resume marks the run COMPLETE on any 'completed' status (ralph_resume.py:83).
principle_conflict: P4/P5: completion without a verification receipt
Z4: a model verdict certifies completion
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: in G1, 'complete' exists only as the output of the Stop gate with a bound receipt. Dispatch or a judge pass is never completion.

atoms.name: Generational spec rewriting by Wonder and Reflect
atoms.statement: 'Gets smarter on its own' concretely means that each generation one LLM (Wonder) asks what is still unknown and another (Reflect) patches the goal, constraints, AC wording and ontology, while the executor rewrites workspace code; the harness never rewrites its own prompts, skills, agents or code and keeps no cross-run lesson memory.
atoms.mechanism: The Wonder prompt is at wonder.py:316 and the Reflect prompt at reflect.py:639. generate_from_reflect takes the refined goal and constraints (seed_generator.py:1802, 1836). AC patch operations are limited to keep/revise/add, with protected ACs locked (reflect.py:66, 996), and agent prompts are loaded read-only (agents/loader.py:28). However, a caller can inject seed_content into an existing lineage (step_seed.py:61), validator repair runs an agent with bypassed permissions (mcp/server/adapter.py:2142), and the README disclaims self-modification (README.md:124).
principle_conflict: PH: G1 does not make the AI smarter
P4/Z1: the spec being judged is rewritten by the model being judged (moving goalposts)
P2: it replaces the native agent workflow
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Not adopted. G1 treats any change to the spec as a new task contract.

atoms.name: QA judge pass ends loop as completed
atoms.statement: The Ralph loop checks 'qa passed' (an LLM score >= 0.80) before the evolve step's action, so a judge pass ends the loop as completed even when the deterministic convergence gate returned 'continue'; when QA is skipped, reaching max generations can also report completed.
atoms.mechanism: The _qa_passed check is at ralph_loop.py:303-306, and passed = score >= pass_threshold at qa.py:639. The threshold of 0.80 is set at evolution_handlers.py:1061, and QA runs whenever the action is 'continue' or 'converged' (evolution_handlers.py:1135). The max-generations branch is at ralph_loop.py:344.
principle_conflict: Z1/Z4: a model verdict certifies completion
P4: completion without deterministic verification
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson for G1's Stop controller: a judge score may only add a 'continue' reason (a veto), never end the continuation chain as success. The only success exit is the deterministic gate.

atoms.name: Convergence needs full verdict coverage
atoms.statement: The evolution outcome gate converges only with full Seed-AC verdict coverage, final approval, a passing run verdict, no regression and a validator receipt. Ontology similarity >= 0.95 alone yields the non-success ONTOLOGY_STABLE, and per-AC rows may veto approval but never mint it.
atoms.mechanism: The outcome gate is at convergence.py:99-116 and 394-434, and the ontology-only branch at convergence.py:300. Per-AC rows are veto-only (core/lineage.py:258), coverage is validated at evaluation_coverage.py:26, and the similarity formula is at core/lineage.py:389. Gap: frozen ACs carry forward earlier PASS rows (focus.py:56), and prose ACs get verification_status 'assumed' (parallel_executor.py:4243).
principle_conflict: P4: verdicts carried forward for frozen ACs are not re-run at the end
atoms.proof_purpose: Stopping because nothing changes is distinguishable from completion; completion needs a verdict for every AC row.
atoms.g1_design: G1's Stop controller has distinct terminal reasons: complete, stagnant, oscillating, budget-exhausted. Only 'complete' requires the full AC pass vector, from a fresh G1 run on the final tree, with no carried-forward verdicts.

atoms.name: Period-2 oscillation, plateau and repetition detection
atoms.statement: Stop detectors include period-2 oscillation (N~=N-2 and N-1~=N-3), a score plateau (|delta| < 0.01 over 3 generations), >= 70% repeated questions, a SHA-256 over structured QA findings that repeats across a window, and strictly decreasing QA grades. The 4-pattern StagnationDetector library is not wired into production.
atoms.mechanism: The detectors are _check_oscillation (convergence.py:557-580), _check_evaluation_plateau (447-463) and _check_repetitive_feedback (582-603), which iterates completed[-3:] including the current generation (596). Ralph adds the findings hash (ralph_loop.py:461) and grade-regression check (ralph_loop.py:540). StagnationDetector's thresholds (resilience/stagnation.py:168) are only exported (resilience/__init__.py:55).
principle_conflict: Mathematics placement: thresholds over model-authored structures (ontology similarity, question text) are not G1 control vectors
atoms.proof_purpose: The continuation loop has returned to an earlier pass/fail state, so further continues are not making progress.
atoms.g1_design: Apply the period-2 rule and the findings-hash idea to G1's own pass/fail vector (Hamming distance and exact revisits of a vector), never to similarity of model text.

atoms.name: Loop budget and policy snapshotted durably
atoms.statement: The automatic Ralph generation budget is clamped to 1..10 and is snapshotted, together with the auto-evolve decision, when evaluation is enqueued, then durably bound to the lineage so later config changes cannot rewrite replay; explicit Ralph requests outside 1..10 are rejected.
atoms.mechanism: Config bounds and the clamp are at config/models.py:297 and 316. snapshot_auto_evolve_policy is at evaluation_job.py:128, the durable budget binding at evaluate_ralph_chain.py:298, and range rejection at ralph_handlers.py:284. The design note is at implementation.md:53.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 bounded loops (adds a durable budget snapshot at admission)
atoms.proof_purpose: The continuation budget in force for a task is the one recorded when the task was admitted.
atoms.g1_design: Bind the maximum number of Stop continuations (at most agy's 10) and the policy digest into the task contract at admission. Stop reads the budget from the ledger, not from live config, and out-of-range values are rejected, not clamped.

atoms.name: Cooperative cancellation, zero-disables caps, uncounted failures
atoms.statement: Watchdogs cancel cooperatively; the generation safety timeout and the MCP tool timeout default to 0 (off); failed generations reuse their number and never count toward the 30-generation cap; rewind resets the cap; and hard token/dollar caps are explicitly rejected.
atoms.mechanism: Cancellation is a cooperative task.cancel() (watchdog.py:143), and the zero defaults are at config/models.py:474. A failed generation reuses its number (loop_support.py:952) and always maps to a RETRY directive (directive_mapping.py:44). Rewind resets the lineage status (projector.py:207), the RFC rejects hard caps (frugality-control-loop.md:240), and the rate limiter force-reserves after a bounded wait (rate_limit.py:197).
principle_conflict: P4/TW: unbounded or cooperative-only bounds can loop or hang
T1 already has hard bounded loops and process-tree reaping
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: every G1 bound is hard and counted (failed turns consume budget), cancellation reaps process trees, and 0 never means unlimited.

atoms.name: Day-old model findings reused without revalidation
atoms.statement: Interview advisory lanes reuse findings that other sessions published within a rolling 1-day window (up to 20 per lane), explicitly without re-establishing that a finding still holds.
atoms.mechanism: The docstring states that freshness is the window and nothing else (recent_findings.py:44-46). RECENT_FINDINGS_WINDOW is one day (recent_findings.py:71), and entries are capped at 20 (recent_findings.py:93).
principle_conflict: P3: memory is never state
Z4: model output is reused as fact
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Not adopted.

atoms.name: Model-built checks and verdicts that certify
atoms.statement: Outside the veto-only pipeline, models build or deliver the checks that certify. The evolve spec verifier passes an AC when LLM-extracted regex assertions match the source and the agent claims a pass. A decomposition-attestation LLM certifies that children cover their parent, so the parent succeeds when all children do. Plugin-mode evaluation returns a host subagent's free-text verdict as final.
atoms.mechanism: The extractor prompt is at verification/extractor.py:37; patterns that match the empty string are refused (verifier.py:953), and a PASS is issued when every assertion is VERIFIED (spec_verification_adapter.py:214-237). The attestation is at parallel_executor.py:7196 and parent success = all children at 6073; TOO_BIG admission requires attempt evidence, but has_remaining_scope comes from the LLM (failure_taxonomy.py:479; parallel_executor.py:6311). Plugin delegation is at evaluation_handlers.py:694, and the evaluator prompt tells the model to run Stage 1 itself (evaluator.md:49).
principle_conflict: Z1/Z4: the check that grants acceptance is model output
P4: no deterministic verification run by the harness
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: G1 may let a model propose a check, but a proposed check gains authority only after deterministic admission (OUR-12, OUR-13), and a model-authored check may only veto.

atoms.name: Retry-driven model, effort and harness escalation
atoms.statement: On retries the orchestrator escalates model tiers (frugal, standard, frontier) and effort, walks Routing D one candidate route per classified failure (at most 128), and may redispatch a failing AC once to a different runtime; 'downgrade after 5 successes' and the N-version tournament are not wired.
atoms.mechanism: Escalation notches are computed at model_routing.py:486. MAX_ROUTE_ATTEMPTS is at route_escalation.py:40 and the attempt walk at 611. One alternate-harness redispatch per AC is allowed (cross_harness_redispatch.py:32). downgrade_success_streak is never consumed (config/models.py:115), the tournament is scaffolding only (n_version_tournament.py:1), and the README still advertises a PAL router (README.md:489).
principle_conflict: P2: changes the native agent's model and effort
P7: model and harness choice become part of control semantics
G1 fixes effort at high, so escalation does not apply
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Not adopted.

atoms.name: One-winner guard tables for terminal events
atoms.statement: Session start, session terminal and per-(generation, root) final acceptance are each appended in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction together with a guard-table insert. The acceptance row is keyed by a SHA-256 of the full payload, so a different digest raises an error instead of overwriting.
atoms.mechanism: The guarded appends are _append_session_start_if_absent_unfenced (event_store.py:898), _append_session_terminal_if_active_unfenced (1022) and _append_ac_acceptance_in_transaction (1212). The latter uses _acceptance_payload_digest (183).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 completion gate binding the receipt sequence and hash (adds an exactly-once guard)
atoms.proof_purpose: A task completes at most once, and with exactly one receipt digest.
atoms.g1_design: The ledger's completion record is unique per task id. A second completion with a different receipt digest is a hard conflict surfaced to the next session, not an overwrite.

atoms.name: Journal reducer re-derives decisions, never more favourable
atoms.statement: The check-package journal accepts only closed record schemas allowed by a phase-transition table, runs the same reducer on write and on replay, and re-derives each recorded status from the recorded observations, refusing any decision more favourable than those observations support.
atoms.mechanism: The Phase enum and TRANSITIONS table are at ledger.py:457 and 1236, and advance passes every record through the validate_record gateway (1333-1347). The same reducer runs on write (1419) and on replay via verify_boundary_order (1778). _supported enforces 'more cautious, never more favourable' (1153-1233), and the closed record types are listed at events.py:1011.
principle_conflict: P3: Ouroboros has no hash chain or anchor beneath it; it must be combined with T1's hash-chained ledger
atoms.proof_purpose: Every stored verdict can be reproduced from stored G1 observations, and none is more favourable than they support.
atoms.g1_design: On replay (at SessionStart and Stop), G1 folds ledger records through a closed-schema transition table and recomputes each completion verdict from the observation records it references. A mismatch marks the task UNDECIDABLE, which blocks completion, rather than trusting the stored verdict.

atoms.name: Unchained event log with wall-clock order
atoms.statement: The SQLite events table is append-only only by convention: there are no triggers, hash chain or MAC. Replay orders by (timestamp, random UUID) while cursors use rowid, malformed rows are skipped on replay, and one UPDATE exists. Checkpoints silently start fresh if every level is corrupt, and deleting every boundary record makes the run read as 'off'.
atoms.mechanism: The schema is at schema.py:42. Replay ordering is at event_store.py:1713, while the cursor uses rowid (1728), and the UPDATE is at picker_index_provisioning.py:263. Malformed rows are skipped (test_event_store.py:2945), and SQLite runs with synchronous=NORMAL (sqlite_connection.py:19). The checkpoint fresh start is at checkpoint.py:684, absence reads as off at boundary/resume.py:63 and ledger.py:1919, and the RFC admits there is no append sequence (contract-ledger.md:114).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 hash-chained append-only ledger with head anchor (this is a weaker form)
principle_conflict: P3: tampering or deletion cannot be told apart from absence
P5: receipts cannot be anchored
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Keep T1's hash chain plus a head anchor outside the workspace so that 'no ledger' and 'deleted ledger' can be told apart. Order by append sequence, not wall clock.

atoms.name: Database-clock lease with self-fencing single writer
atoms.statement: Generation ownership uses a 300 s lease acquired under BEGIN IMMEDIATE and measured on the database clock. The owner fences itself at half the lease, expired leases are reclaimed in two phases, and every owned write checks the fencing token and inserts the event in one transaction.
atoms.mechanism: DEFAULT_LEASE_SECONDS is at generation_claims.py:65 and BEGIN IMMEDIATE at 144. _db_now reads the time via julianday (245), the fenced append is at 299-337, and the half-lease fence at 551. Lineage advancement claims, by contrast, use the wall clock and require explicit operator recovery (lineage_claims.py:39, 767).
principle_conflict: P8: needed only if G1 hook processes can write concurrently (the global and workspace layers both run)
atoms.proof_purpose: At most one writer appended to the task ledger at a time, so receipts are never interleaved.
atoms.g1_design: If G1's global and workspace hook layers can append concurrently, guard ledger appends with a flock or SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE lease and check a fencing token inside the append transaction. An expired owner is never taken over implicitly.

atoms.name: Boot-id process identity and flock leases
atoms.statement: A session owner's liveness is proven by a held flock plus a persisted (boot_id, pid, start_ticks) identity that rejects PID reuse and processes from a prior boot; sessions idle for an hour without a live lease are cancelled at server start.
atoms.mechanism: current_persisted_process_identity is at persisted_process_identity.py:65-85, and the flock-held lease at heartbeat.py:264-315. The orphan sweep is at session.py:1543.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 process-tree reaping (adds an identity that is safe against PID reuse)
atoms.proof_purpose: A recorded process owner is the same process, not a recycled PID.
atoms.g1_design: Record (boot_id, pid, start_ticks) for every process G1 spawns or tracks, and check that triple before reaping a process or declaring an owner dead.

atoms.name: Resume authority is process-local
atoms.statement: A fresh process can rebuild a session's status from the event store but cannot resume the work: execution authority belongs to the process that started it, a new process gets 'process-local resume unavailable', and status reconstruction ignores failures reading related events by default.
atoms.mechanism: The refusal is raised by _process_local_resume_unavailable_error (runner.py:4528-4543). Only same-process resume is supported (test_session_persistence.py:363), and reconstruction is best-effort (session.py:1342).
principle_conflict: P1/TW-b: a fresh agent must continue durable work from G1 facts alone
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: every piece of G1 authority (task, budget, receipts) can be reconstructed from the ledger alone.

atoms.name: Policy sealed per run, drift refused
atoms.statement: Each run seals its verification policy (run_verify_commands, exec_sandbox_enabled, verify timeout, verify-shell identity, retries, decomposition) into a versioned execution-semantics contract that resume validates exactly, and the executor re-checks the code identity of the verifier, dispatcher and coordinator before each effect.
atoms.mechanism: The exact-key contract is validated by valid_execution_semantics_contract (execution_semantics.py:111) and built from runner state (runner.py:3937); the sandbox policy is sealed into it (verifier-evidence-policy.md:170). Code identity is captured at execution_authority.py:2838, and 'execution authority drifted before effect' is raised at parallel_executor.py:1241. The code itself says this is not a boundary against code in the same process (execution_authority.py:103), and older contracts migrate with verify_shell_identity unset (execution_semantics.py:173).
principle_conflict: P5: Ouroboros seals policy into the session contract but not into each check receipt
atoms.proof_purpose: The receipt was produced under exactly the verification policy the task was admitted with.
atoms.g1_design: At admission, G1 hashes its active policy (hooks.json files, check-runner version, sandbox state, budgets) into the task contract and into every receipt. A policy-digest mismatch at Stop blocks completion until a new task contract is admitted.

atoms.name: Extension trust keyed to tree digest
atoms.statement: A UserLevel plugin is trusted by (source, identity, canonical tree hash), and the firewall recomputes the tree hash before every invocation, failing closed with trust_subject_changed if it differs; the verify shell's identity is captured the same way.
atoms.mechanism: The digest module is plugin/digest.py:1-15. The note that the firewall recomputes the tree hash and fails closed is at plugin/trust_store.py:39-43. The verify shell's identity is captured at verify_shell.py:245.
atoms.proof_purpose: The hook scripts and check runner executing now are byte-identical to the ones the root of trust approved.
atoms.g1_design: The global root-of-trust file records the SHA-256 of every G1 hook script and of the workspace hooks.json. Each hook invocation, or at least SessionStart, recomputes them. On a mismatch, PreToolUse denies mutating tools and the Stop gate refuses completion, because the agent can rewrite hooks.json for the next session.

atoms.name: Advisory fail-open hooks, no PreToolUse/Stop
atoms.statement: Ouroboros' host hooks are SessionStart (PyPI update notice), UserPromptSubmit (keyword-to-skill injection via additionalContext) and PostToolUse on Write|Edit (an mtime-based 'drift' notice). All of them exit 0 on failure, none is a PreToolUse or Stop gate, and the repo-local hook commands fall back to $PWD for the script root.
atoms.mechanism: The hook events are declared at hooks/hooks.json:3, 16 and 29. The update check is at scripts/session-start.py:24, context emission at keyword-detector.py:306, and the drift check at drift-monitor.py:31. The $PWD fallback is at .claude/settings.json:8, and the only PreToolUse is an in-process SDK hook that rewrites delegated tool input (orchestrator/adapter.py:1633).
principle_conflict: P4/P6: enforcement lives in an orchestrator the user must drive, not in hooks
Z6: a hook script resolved from the workspace ($PWD) is writable by the agent
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Lesson: G1 hook commands use absolute paths under the root of trust, never $PWD or a workspace-relative script root. Injection hooks stay fail-open; gates stay fail-closed.

atoms.name: Veto hooks fail closed, observe hooks fail open
atoms.statement: The plugin tool-call hook contract separates an intercept scope, which may veto and fails closed by default, from an observe scope, which may only watch and fails open; the firewall treats a nonzero intercept result as a block.
atoms.mechanism: The permission scopes are defined in the RFC (plugin-tool-call-hook-contract.md:69-96). They are enforced by dispatch_before_tool_call and dispatch_after_tool_call (firewall.py:2066, 2285), using the hook kinds at plugin/hooks.py:84.
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:T1 fail-closed gates and fail-open projection
atoms.proof_purpose: A crashed or timed-out gate never lets a tool call through, and a crashed observer never blocks one.
atoms.g1_design: T1 already has this rule. Map it onto agy: PreToolUse gates print deny or nothing (never allow, and {} counts as deny), and injection hooks are fail-open.

atoms.name: agy driven headless with full skip-permissions
atoms.statement: When Ouroboros drives Antigravity, it runs `agy -p <prompt> --dangerously-skip-permissions [--model]` with the prompt in argv and reads plain-text stdout that has no structured tool events. It translates tool restrictions into prompt prose, forces bypass on every orchestrated runtime, parses stdout JSON-first (so the model can forge events), skips binary-identity checks, and the check-package constructor refuses agy.
atoms.mechanism: The command is built at antigravity_cli_runtime.py:159-168, and every permission mode collapses to the skip flag (antigravity_cli_runtime.py:59). Capabilities declare structured_output=False and TRANSLATED tool restrictions (209-216), and bypass is forced at runner.py:791 and 967. Stdout is parsed JSON-first (gemini_event_normalizer.py:149) and the prompt travels in argv (gemini_cli_runtime.py:322). The exact-type trusted-runtime list excludes agy (runner.py:4058), the constructor's backend allowlist refuses it (constructor_session.py:48), and the docs carry a warning (antigravity.md:111).
principle_conflict: Z4/Z5: stdout from the model is parsed as protocol
P4: this integration gets no structured tool evidence from agy print mode
atoms.proof_purpose: none (host facts for G1's agy adapter)
atoms.g1_design: Facts for G1's agy adapter: tool restrictions stated in the prompt are not enforcement, so G1 must deny in PreToolUse. G1 takes tool evidence from hook stdin and transcriptPath, never from agy stdout. Re-test these claims against agy 1.1.27 before relying on them.

atoms.name: Host text quarantined from failure classifiers
atoms.statement: In host-dispatch mode, a failure reported by the host is kept as data and the terminal message content is replaced with a fixed string, so host text such as 'usage limit reached' cannot steer the engine's recovery classifiers; empty or non-substantive submissions are rejected.
atoms.mechanism: The failure branch keeps the host's words out of the terminal content (host_dispatch.py:625-643), and submissions are validated at host_dispatch.py:760-781. On success, however, the content still comes from host text (host_dispatch.py:616).
atoms.novelty: duplicate-of:vesperchant 00-instinct trusted channel versus data channel
atoms.proof_purpose: No control decision (pause, retry, budget) was triggered by text the model wrote.
atoms.g1_design: G1 classifies outcomes only from hook event fields and the exit codes of checks G1 ran. Model and tool text goes into the ledger as quoted data and is never pattern-matched to choose a control action.

atoms.name: Paired counterbalanced A/B experiment harness
atoms.statement: A manual canonical harness runs paired arms in x/y, y/x, x/y order from a frozen ledger, with preflight hashes of the source tree, expected.yaml and model config. A deterministic smoke oracle grades each arm, the decision is a vote count with no statistics, and the only committed run is inconclusive because all pairs were invalid.
atoms.mechanism: The pair orders are _PAIR_ORDERS (test_issue_1450_quality.py:45), with preflight hashing at 381-420 and oracle_pass at 709. _pair_outcome (723) and _decide (743) produce the verdict. The committed report is REPORT.md:5, the oracle is defined in cli-todo/expected.yaml:24, and the harness is manual-only (canonical/README.md:9).
principle_conflict: Mathematics placement: no paired statistics or intervals; the validity filter discards pipeline failures; the oracle cannot be derived from what the arms see; the runner does not wait for detached work
atoms.proof_purpose: none in the authority path; in measurement it would show whether an injected rule changes outcomes
atoms.g1_design: Reuse the shape for G1's A/B tests of injected content: paired counterbalanced arms, preflight hashes that include the grader file, and a deterministic oracle. Add exact sign or McNemar tests with confidence intervals and pre-registered sample sizes, and count pipeline failures as outcomes.

atoms.name: Anti-skip assertions, positive controls and audit canaries
atoms.statement: The tests guard against vacuous passes: CI fails if named native tests were skipped, a test asserts that Landlock really exists on the Linux CI runner, a real outbound connection serves as a positive control before network denial is asserted, a CPython audit hook with planted canary files (and a negative control) proves the controller reads only declared inputs, and real LLM spawning is blocked in tests.
atoms.mechanism: The Windows anti-skip step is at test.yml:156-167, the Landlock existence test at test_exec_sandbox.py:532 and the positive network control at test_exec_sandbox.py:362. The controller-isolation canaries are at test_controller_isolation.py:1 and 147, and the fixture blocking LLM and CLI spawns at tests/conftest.py:154. The acceptance-authority test loops exhaustively over model verdicts (test_pipeline_acceptance_authority.py:271).
atoms.proof_purpose: A passing G1 conformance suite actually exercised each mechanism (no vacuous skip), and a positive control showed the check could fail.
atoms.g1_design: Every G1 host-contract re-test and conformance test includes a positive control (the bad action succeeds without G1), a negative control (G1 blocks it), and an assertion that the environment supports the mechanism, so an unsupported environment fails the test rather than skipping it.

atoms.name: Bot review approval satisfies required review
atoms.statement: The repository's one required approving review can be satisfied by the ouroboros-agent bot, and agent handoff docs say to merge only after the bot approves, so a model's verdict is part of the merge path.
atoms.mechanism: The branch-protection note is at ci-gates.md:32 and the handoff instruction at handoff-auto-contract-ac-grounding-2026-07.md:226. The bot's verdict format is described in review-conventions.md:28.
principle_conflict: Z1/Z4: a model verdict certifies a merge
atoms.proof_purpose: none
atoms.g1_design: Not adopted.

adoption_candidates: OUR-01: The single veto-only acceptance function is exactly G1's 'model may veto, never certify' rule, and it comes with an exhaustive test to port.
OUR-12: Red-before-green admission proves each check discriminates; it is the missing half of G1's coverage-matrix contract check.
OUR-08: Keeping check text out of the agent's context and readable files removes the cheapest reward-hacking path, and G1 can enforce it with PreToolUse denies.
OUR-46: A reducer that re-derives every stored verdict from stored observations ('never more favourable') hardens P3/P5 on top of T1's hash chain.
OUR-22: Hash-pinned executables plus an allowlisted environment let the receipt bind the exact binary and environment that produced it.
OUR-02: The tri-state APPROVED/REJECTED/UNVERIFIED keeps 'no evidence' from ever rendering as a pass.
OUR-26: The per-AC verify-command gate becomes G1's zero-row contract rejection once it is block-only and fails closed.
OUR-23: A tree digest around every write-capable step, with model self-reports never counted as proof, binds the verified tree to the delivered tree.
OUR-13: The unparseable-target canary is a cheap mutation test proving a check depends on the file it claims to test.
OUR-30: Workspace-sourced config cannot change execution, which maps directly onto G1's global root-of-trust versus the workspace .agents/hooks.json.
OUR-51: Sealing the verification policy per task and refusing drift binds the policy itself into P5 receipts.
OUR-14: Re-running pre-existing tests from base bytes against the candidate defeats test deletion or editing as a deterministic veto.
OUR-24: One-to-one call-id correlation of tool start and completion gives forgery-resistant PostToolUse evidence.
OUR-58: Anti-skip assertions, positive controls and audit-hook canaries make G1's conformance and host-contract tests self-proving.
OUR-56: Model or host text never selects a control action, so 'usage limit reached'-style steering is impossible.
OUR-40: Snapshot the Stop-continuation budget (at most agy's 10) and the policy at task admission, and read them from the ledger.
OUR-03: Recompute summary verdicts from literal per-check results instead of trusting a stored aggregate.
OUR-52: Digest-bound trust in hook scripts detects an agent rewriting hooks.json before it takes effect in the next session.
OUR-45: An exactly-once completion record keyed by receipt digest turns double completion into a hard conflict.
OUR-38: Distinct terminal reasons ensure 'stable/stagnant' is never mistaken for 'complete'.
risks: Telemetry is on by default: PostHog with an embedded project key (src/ouroboros/telemetry.py:49) sends to https://us.i.posthog.com (src/ouroboros/telemetry.py:50); the default is set at src/ouroboros/config/models.py:805 and the identity is a random UUID in ~/.ouroboros/telemetry.json (src/ouroboros/telemetry.py:9). The installer also pings install_started via curl (scripts/install.sh:894). Opt out with DO_NOT_TRACK or OUROBOROS_TELEMETRY=0.
Network calls without an opt-out: the SessionStart hook fetches PyPI JSON (scripts/version-check.py:150), and skills tell the agent to curl the GitHub releases API (skills/interview/SKILL.md:57).

Supply chain: the repo's .mcp.json and .codex/config.toml launch an unpinned `uvx --from ouroboros-ai[mcp]` on every MCP start (.mcp.json:10, .codex/config.toml:8). The installer is curl|bash (scripts/install.sh:3), silently adds the Claude plugin marketplace and installs the plugin (scripts/install.sh:1514), and the setup skill falls back to curl|sh for astral uv (skills/setup/SKILL.md:205).

Prompt-steering text reaches host models. The MCP server instructions say to use Ouroboros BEFORE implementation, not to wait for 'ooo', and to never surface the tool-discovery plumbing to the user (src/ouroboros/backends/capabilities.py:765, src/ouroboros/backends/capabilities.py:785). The UserPromptSubmit hook injects skill suggestions and first-time welcome directives (scripts/keyword-detector.py:306, scripts/keyword-detector.py:336). Skills ask the agent to star the repo through `gh api -X PUT /user/starred/Q00/ouroboros` behind a user prompt (skills/setup/SKILL.md:125, skills/welcome/SKILL.md:1073, skills/seed/SKILL.md:469).

Execution privilege: OrchestratorRunner forces bypassPermissions on every runtime (src/ouroboros/orchestrator/runner.py:791), and agy runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions (src/ouroboros/orchestrator/antigravity_cli_runtime.py:163). MCP auth defaults to NONE, which grants every permission (src/ouroboros/mcp/server/security.py:59).

Secrets exposure: the hidden verify gate and Stage-1 checks run agent-written code with the controller environment, including API keys (src/ouroboros/orchestrator/verify_shell.py:441, src/ouroboros/evaluation/mechanical.py:120). Vendor CLIs inherit all of os.environ (src/ouroboros/runtime/child_env.py:67), and the IOJournal stores prompt and tool previews by default (src/ouroboros/events/io.py:23).

Judge prompt injection and exfiltration: agent-controlled artifact text is fenced only with ``` inside judge prompts (src/ouroboros/evaluation/semantic.py:170), and the evaluation judge may use WebFetch/WebSearch for up to 20 turns (src/ouroboros/mcp/tools/evaluation_handlers.py:783, src/ouroboros/orchestrator/policy.py:118). The citation checker fetches host-supplied URLs with scheme-only validation, an SSRF risk (src/ouroboros/mcp/tools/citation_check.py:94).
Prompt override: OUROBOROS_AGENTS_DIR replaces every agent and judge prompt (src/ouroboros/agents/loader.py:39).

Hidden-grader leakage: verify_command is persisted in event payloads in a SQLite file the worker's user can read (src/ouroboros/orchestrator/parallel_executor.py:9980), and retry hints forward verifier output tails (src/ouroboros/orchestrator/retry_hints.py:120).

Ledger integrity: the event log is unauthenticated, writable by the same user and contains an in-place UPDATE (src/ouroboros/persistence/picker_index_provisioning.py:263). SQLite runs with synchronous=NORMAL (src/ouroboros/persistence/sqlite_connection.py:19), and the checkpoint hash is unkeyed (src/ouroboros/persistence/checkpoint.py:30).

Fail-open acceptance paths that a worker can trigger: a verify-gate timeout is quarantined as success (src/ouroboros/orchestrator/parallel_executor.py:9830), and criteria with no evidence are accepted (src/ouroboros/boundary/acceptance.py:796).
Destructive legacy script: scripts/ralph.sh commits with `git add -A` (scripts/ralph.sh:128) and rolls back with `git clean -fd` (scripts/ralph.sh:165), which can lose untracked work.
Delegated runs take the parent transcript path, cwd and permission mode from MCP tool input without provenance checks (src/ouroboros/mcp/tools/execution_handlers.py:640).

Quality and doc drift: the README advertises a PAL router, auto-downgrade, 4-pattern stagnation detection and drift gating that are removed or unwired (README.md:489, src/ouroboros/resilience/__init__.py:55). The judge prompt claims empty evidence fails verification, but the parser accepts it (src/ouroboros/evaluation/semantic.py:203, src/ouroboros/evaluation/semantic.py:283). The e2e tests mock the model boundary (tests/e2e/conftest.py:165).
Platform: the sandbox needs Landlock ABI 3 or later (src/ouroboros/runtime/_confine_exec.py:131); under PRoot-like hosts, replay and check packages fail closed or are skipped.
